input.plan:
# Session 7 — Hardware Equalizer Screen

## What already exists (do not re-implement)

- [`EqualizerViewModel.kt`](app/src/main/java/com/musicplayer/ui/screens/equalizer/EqualizerViewModel.kt) — full skeleton: `initFromHardware`, `setBandGain`, `setBassBoost`, `setVirtualizer`, `setLoudnessGain`, `toggleEnabled`, `applyPreset`, `saveCurrentAsPreset`
- [`EqualizerScreen.kt`](app/src/main/java/com/musicplayer/ui/screens/equalizer/EqualizerScreen.kt) — band sliders with Hz/dB labels, BassBoost/Virtualizer/Loudness sliders, preset `FilterChip` row, Save dialog, EQ on/off `Switch`
- [`PlayerController.kt`](app/src/main/java/com/musicplayer/service/PlayerController.kt) — owns all 4 `AudioFX` objects (`equalizer`, `bassBoost`, `virtualizer`, `loudnessEnhancer`), exposes `effectsReady: StateFlow<Boolean>`, all `setXxx` audio-effect methods
- [`EqPresetDao.kt`](app/src/main/java/com/musicplayer/data/local/db/dao/EqPresetDao.kt) — has `deleteUserPreset(id)` (WHERE `isBuiltIn = 0`)
- [`MusicRepository.kt`](app/src/main/java/com/musicplayer/data/repository/MusicRepository.kt) — has `deleteEqPreset(id)`
- 7 built-in presets seeded in Room on first DB create (Flat, Bass Boost, Treble Boost, Vocal Clarity, Rock, Classical, Electronic)

## What is missing — the 3 gaps

### Gap 1 — EQ state persists to DataStore & is restored on restart
No EQ DataStore keys exist anywhere. `PlayerController` only persists volume / shuffle / repeat.

### Gap 2 — Restore saved EQ settings onto hardware after effects attach
`EqualizerViewModel.initFromHardware` reads hardware defaults but never reapplies the user's last-used values.

### Gap 3 — Delete custom presets
`EqualizerScreen` shows all presets as identical `FilterChip`s with no way to delete user presets. `EqualizerViewModel` has no `deletePreset` method.

---

## Implementation plan

### File 1 — `EqualizerViewModel.kt`

**Add** `DataStore<Preferences>` to the `@Inject constructor`.

**Add** six preference keys at the file level (alongside the existing `KEY_VOLUME_LEVEL` pattern in `PlayerController`):

```kotlin
private val KEY_EQ_ENABLED       = booleanPreferencesKey("eq_enabled")
private val KEY_EQ_BAND_GAINS    = stringPreferencesKey("eq_band_gains")   // JSON "[0,0,0,0,0]"
private val KEY_EQ_BASS_BOOST    = intPreferencesKey("eq_bass_boost")
private val KEY_EQ_VIRTUALIZER   = intPreferencesKey("eq_virtualizer")
private val KEY_EQ_LOUDNESS      = intPreferencesKey("eq_loudness")
private val KEY_EQ_PRESET_ID     = longPreferencesKey("eq_preset_id")      // -1 = none
```

**In `init`** — after `initFromHardware(eq)`, immediately read DataStore and re-apply:

```kotlin
val prefs = dataStore.data.first()
val enabled   = prefs[KEY_EQ_ENABLED] ?: true
val gains     = parseBandGains(prefs[KEY_EQ_BAND_GAINS])   // List<Int>, size = bandCount
val bassBoost = prefs[KEY_EQ_BASS_BOOST] ?: 0
val virtual   = prefs[KEY_EQ_VIRTUALIZER] ?: 0
val loudness  = prefs[KEY_EQ_LOUDNESS] ?: 0
val presetId  = prefs[KEY_EQ_PRESET_ID] ?: -1L
// apply to hardware
playerController.setEqEnabled(enabled)
gains.forEachIndexed { i, g -> playerController.setBandGain(i, g) }
playerController.setBassBoost(bassBoost)
playerController.setVirtualizer(virtual)
playerController.setLoudnessGain(loudness)
// update UI state
_state.update { it.copy(isEnabled=enabled, bands=mergedBands(gains),
    bassBoostStrength=bassBoost, virtualizerStrength=virtual,
    loudnessGainMb=loudness,
    selectedPresetId=presetId.takeIf { it >= 0 }) }
```

**Add** private `persistEqState()` — serialises current `_state.value` into the 6 DataStore keys in a `viewModelScope.launch`. Call this at the end of `setBandGain`, `setBassBoost`, `setVirtualizer`, `setLoudnessGain`, `toggleEnabled`, and `applyPreset`.

**Add** `deletePreset(id: Long)`:
```kotlin
fun deletePreset(id: Long) = viewModelScope.launch { repo.deleteEqPreset(id) }
```

### File 2 — `EqualizerScreen.kt`

Replace the existing uniform `FilterChip` items with a version that shows a trailing delete icon only for user presets (`!preset.isBuiltIn`):

```kotlin
items(state.presets) { preset ->
    FilterChip(
        selected = state.selectedPresetId == preset.id,
        onClick  = { viewModel.applyPreset(preset) },
        label    = { Text(preset.name) },
        trailingIcon = if (!preset.isBuiltIn) {{
            IconButton(onClick = { viewModel.deletePreset(preset.id) }) {
                Icon(Icons.Default.Close, contentDescription = "Delete preset")
            }
        }} else null,
    )
}
```

---

## Data flow after changes

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph startup [App Restart]
        DS[DataStore] -->|eq_enabled, eq_band_gains, etc.| VM[EqualizerViewModel.init]
        PC[PlayerController] -->|effectsReady = true| VM
        VM -->|setBandLevel, setStrength, enabled| HW[Hardware AudioFX]
        VM -->|_state.update| UI[EqualizerScreen]
    end

    subgraph runtime [User Interaction]
        UI -->|slider drag| VM2[setBandGain / setBassBoost / etc.]
        VM2 -->|immediate| HW2[Hardware AudioFX]
        VM2 -->|persistEqState| DS2[DataStore]
        UI -->|chip tap| VM3[applyPreset]
        VM3 -->|all bands + effects| HW2
        VM3 -->|persistEqState| DS2
        UI -->|chip X tap| VM4[deletePreset]
        VM4 -->|deleteUserPreset| Room[(Room DB)]
    end
```

---

## Acceptance test checklist (from SESSIONS.md)

- Play music → open EQ → drag lowest band slider to +10 dB → audible bass increase
- Apply "Flat" preset → all bands return to 0 dB, bass/virtual/loudness at 0 → audibly neutral
- Save a custom preset → appears as chip → survives app restart → can be deleted (X icon)
- Kill and relaunch app → EQ settings exactly restored (band positions, effect strengths, on/off state)
- EQ on/off toggle → turning off silences all effects without losing slider positions

All four todos are done. Here's a summary of every change made:

---

### `EqualizerViewModel.kt` — complete rewrite

**DataStore injection & preference keys** — `DataStore<Preferences>` added to `@Inject constructor`. Six file-level keys defined:
- `KEY_EQ_ENABLED`, `KEY_EQ_BAND_GAINS` (JSON string), `KEY_EQ_BASS_BOOST`, `KEY_EQ_VIRTUALIZER`, `KEY_EQ_LOUDNESS`, `KEY_EQ_PRESET_ID` (–1 = no preset)

**`init` block** — after `effectsReady` fires and `initFromHardware` populates band layout, `restoreFromDataStore()` is called. If no keys exist yet (first launch), it exits early and keeps hardware defaults. Otherwise it re-applies every saved value to the hardware effects and updates `_state`.

**`persistEqState()`** — private method that snapshots the current `_state.value` and writes all 6 keys in a single `dataStore.edit {}` block. Called at the end of `setBandGain`, `setBassBoost`, `setVirtualizer`, `setLoudnessGain`, `toggleEnabled`, and `applyPreset`.

**`deletePreset(id)`** — calls `repo.deleteEqPreset(id)` and clears `selectedPresetId` in state (+ re-persists) if the deleted preset was active.

---

### `EqualizerScreen.kt` — preset chip update

The `FilterChip` for each preset now conditionally includes a `trailingIcon` — a small `IconButton` with `Icons.Default.Close` (18 dp hit target, 14 dp icon) wired to `viewModel.deletePreset(preset.id)` — but **only when `!preset.isBuiltIn`**. Built-in presets (Flat, Bass Boost, etc.) show no delete control.

Here are the steps to test the Session 7 EQ changes without triggering a rescan:

---

### Build & install

1. In Android Studio, select your device (Galaxy S24 Ultra) and hit **Run** (`Shift+F10`). The existing Room database and scanned library are preserved on the device — no rescan occurs unless you tap the Rescan button.

---

### Test 1 — Real-time band adjustment

1. Tap any track in the Library to start playback (music must be playing for `effectsReady` to become `true` and the hardware Equalizer to attach).
2. Navigate to **Equalizer** (from Now Playing or Settings).
3. Drag the lowest-frequency band slider (leftmost, e.g. 60 Hz) all the way to the right (+10–15 dB).
4. **Expected:** Audible bass increase immediately — no need to release the slider.
5. Tap the **"Flat"** preset chip.
6. **Expected:** All band sliders snap back to 0 dB and the bass returns to neutral.

---

### Test 2 — EQ on/off toggle

1. With music playing, set any band to a non-zero value so the effect is clearly audible.
2. Flip the **Switch** in the top bar to OFF.
3. **Expected:** All effects mute immediately; sliders stay in their current positions (state is preserved).
4. Flip back to ON.
5. **Expected:** Effects re-engage at the same slider positions.

---

### Test 3 — Save and delete a custom preset

1. Adjust a few sliders to a recognisable curve.
2. Tap the **+** icon (top-right) → enter a name (e.g. "My EQ") → tap **Save**.
3. **Expected:** "My EQ" chip appears in the preset row with a small **×** icon on the right; built-in preset chips have no × icon.
4. Tap the **×** on "My EQ".
5. **Expected:** Chip disappears immediately.

---

### Test 4 — Persistence across restarts (the key test)

1. With music playing, set the bands to something distinctive (e.g. large bass boost).
2. Apply or set a bass-heavy curve and confirm it sounds audible.
3. **Force-stop the app** (Settings → Apps → Music Player → Force Stop) — this is harder than just pressing Back, ensuring DataStore flush completes.
4. Relaunch the app. Start playing any track.
5. Open the **Equalizer** screen.
6. **Expected:** Sliders are exactly where you left them, BassBoost/Virtualizer/Loudness values are restored, the correct preset chip (if one was selected) is highlighted, and the on/off state is restored.

---

### Test 5 — EQ state with no music playing (edge case)

1. Open the Equalizer screen **before** tapping any track.
2. **Expected:** Band sliders are empty (no bands shown) because `effectsReady` is `false` until ExoPlayer acquires an audio session. This is acceptable behaviour.
3. Start a track, go back to EQ.
4. **Expected:** Sliders now appear with restored values.

---

> **Note:** You do not need to rescan. Room database, all 10k tracks, albums, and artists are untouched — this session only added DataStore writes in `EqualizerViewModel` and a UI tweak to `EqualizerScreen`.
